column1: # player-vocabulary-allow.tsv — the private-vocabulary words in player copy that STAY, one per row.
# Read by `scripts/check-player-vocabulary.py`. Four TAB-separated fields:
#     path <TAB> term <TAB> the exact text, with \n \t \r \\ escaped <TAB> why the word stays
# ⚑ KEYED BY THE TEXT, NOT THE LINE. Lanes move lines all day; a line-number key rots into a
#   blanket ignore inside a day. Keying on the text is also the ratchet's second edge: a row whose
#   text is no longer at that path FAILS the gate. Fixing a string RETIRES its exemption instead of
#   leaving a permission slip behind for the next `receipt` to walk through.
# ⚑ A ROW IS AN ARGUMENT, NOT A MUTE. The reason field is required and the gate refuses an empty
#   one. "operator output", "a JSON error body", "a test fixture" and "a CSS class name" are NOT
#   reasons to write here: those are rules R3, R5, R2 and R6 inside the checker, and a site of that
#   kind being reported means the RULE is wrong and should be fixed. Two rules were in fact fixed
#   rather than allowlisted while this file was being written (`fhegg_operation.rs` moved to
#   `NOT_PLAYER_SURFACES` because it renders no markup at all; `descent.rs`'s pointer-width refusal
#   was simply rewritten, since "exceeds this executor target" named the wrong limit anyway).
#   What belongs here is a site where the word is doing a job no plain equivalent does.
# ⚑ THIS FILE IS EMPTY, AND EMPTY IS THE CORRECT STATE. It was seeded on 2026-07-26 with SIX rows,
# every one of them opening `DEBT ·` and closing "File held by another lane this pass." — which is
# to say, six pieces of live player copy on `/descent/play` and `/tug` excused for a scheduling
# reason, each carrying the replacement it was waiting for. On 2026-07-27 that excuse was measured
# and had expired, so the six replacements were simply written and the rows retired themselves:
#   descent_play.rs   " · receipt "                    → " · this move recorded as "
#                     "the native executor declined…"  → "the move was re-run in this tab and
#                                                         refused, with no reason given"
#                     "…all N receipts."               → "…all N moves."   (`report.turns` IS moves)
#   tug_web.rs        "the deck, the fog, scoring"     → "the deck, the hidden hand, scoring"
#                     "a conservation tooth the executor enforces"
#                                                      → "That 21 is fixed for the whole round … a
#                                                         move that would do either is refused"
#                     "the executor refuses a claimed win the rules do not make"
#                                                      → "a claimed win the rules do not make is
#                                                         refused"
# ⚠ TWO of those six were ALSO STALE AT THE COMMIT THAT WROTE THEM (`8f0a2312a`). Replaying this
# gate's reader over `git show 8f0a2312a:…` gives 6 rows against 5 live hits, and the two that
# match nothing are both in `tug_web.rs`: the `fog` `<summary>` (at that tree `fog` was in `//!`
# doc comments ONLY, which R1 never yields) and the "names them: 11 influence…" `executor` `<li>`.
# Both were keyed to another lane's UNCOMMITTED working-tree text, which did not land until
# `4bcb934a3` a day later — so a clean checkout of `8f0a2312a` fails this gate on its own
# allowlist. The lesson is not "check harder": a row written for a file you are not editing is a
# row written against a tree you cannot see. Fix the string instead — the fix and the retirement
# are the same edit.
# So: adding a row here is legitimate ONLY for a word doing a job no plain equivalent does. There
# is currently no such word. "Another lane owns the file" is not one of the reasons.
